title: Science or fiction? Shadowy ‘paper mills’ let you pay to be a published author – of fraudulent research

paragraphs.en: Dr Reese Richardson’s phone constantly buzzes with notifications. The scientific research integrity specialist has been tracking shadowy organisations known as “paper mills”, which turn a profit by offering fraudulent academic authorship of scientific papers, IP registrations and other scholarly outputs.
paragraphs.zh: 里斯·理查森博士的手机不断因各种通知而振动。这位科研诚信专家一直在追踪被称为“论文工厂”的隐秘组织，它们靠提供欺诈性的学术论文作者署名、知识产权注册和其他学术产出牟利。

paragraphs.en: For a fee, paper mills offer to list people as authors of scientific journal articles, often of falsified research that bypasses the peer review process.
paragraphs.zh: 只要付费，论文工厂就能把人们列为科学期刊文章的作者，而这些文章往往是绕过同行评审过程的伪造研究。

paragraphs.en: Richardson has joined dozens of groups across apps such as Telegram, WhatsApp and Facebook where a buffet of fraudulent and fabricated research is advertised to hundreds of members. “I can just look through my notifications and I can see that I’ve gotten, like, 20 WhatsApp messages from paper mills in the last 24 hours,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: 理查森加入了Telegram、WhatsApp和Facebook等应用上的数十个群组，在这些群组里，形形色色的欺诈性、捏造性研究被推销给数百名成员。他说：“我只要翻翻自己的通知，就能看到过去24小时里收到了大约20条来自论文工厂的WhatsApp消息。”

paragraphs.en: Scientists are under constant pressure to publish new research papers which, in many parts of the world, remain the currency of academia. They beget more grant funding and accolades, and enhance academic profiles. But robust, high-quality science takes time, and papers can take years to get published.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家始终承受着发表新论文的压力，在世界许多地方，论文仍是学术界的硬通货。它们带来更多的科研经费和荣誉，并提升学术声望。但扎实、高质量的科学研究需要时间，论文可能要数年才能发表。

paragraphs.en: Paper mills offer a fraudulent shortcut, using instant messaging and social media platforms to find prospective buyers looking for papers and patents to stack their CVs. According to an analysis Richardson conducted with Anna Abalkina and Spencer Hong, the median price to buy authorship is around US$800 (A$1,150).
paragraphs.zh: 论文工厂提供了一条欺诈性的捷径，利用即时通讯和社交媒体平台寻找那些想用论文和专利充实简历的潜在买家。根据理查森与安娜·阿巴尔金娜、斯潘塞·洪共同进行的分析，购买作者署名的价格中位数约为800美元（1150澳元）。

paragraphs.en: In a recent paper, which has not yet been peer reviewed, the trio of scientists led by Richardson, formerly at Northwestern University in the US, detailed more than 18,000 advertisements from seven paper mills across seven countries between 2020 and 2026.
paragraphs.zh: 在一篇尚未经过同行评审的最新论文中，以曾任职于美国西北大学的理查森为首的三位科学家，详述了2020年至2026年间来自七个国家七家论文工厂的超过1.8万条广告。

paragraphs.en: Related: Is the staggeringly profitable business of scientific publishing bad for science?
paragraphs.zh: 相关阅读：利润惊人的科学出版业是否对科学有害？

paragraphs.en: “We wanted to get an idea, across a wide range of paper mills, countries, topics and product types how much these things actually go for,” he says. “What we put together is the largest ever dataset of paper mill advertisements.”
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“我们想了解，在广泛的论文工厂、国家、主题和产品类型中，这些东西的售价究竟是多少。我们整理出的是迄今为止最大的论文工厂广告数据集。”
